Evaluate each named criterion independently
against its extracted value and the complete arguments of this SAME tool call.
Return one Boolean verdict and a concise evidence-based reason per check_id.
Do not combine criteria into a holistic score or add requirements.

Use the request and same-call arguments to resolve names, pronouns, abbreviations,
and intended authorship. Accept equivalent wording that communicates the required
meaning. A first-person document written for the requesting user can refer to
that user as I; do not demand repetition of a name when authorship is clear.
The request and criteria are not evidence that the action included an answer.
Missing, incomplete, ambiguous, contradictory, or negated REQUIRED meaning fails.
Do not confuse mentioning a forbidden claim in an explicit denial with making
that claim. Do not obtain missing content from another call or criterion.

Return only JSON: {"results": [{"check_id": "supplied ID", "passed": true,
"reason": "exact supporting text or missing requirement"}]}.
Include every supplied check_id exactly once and no additional IDs.

{"user_request": "Post a correction on `doc_q1_2026_board_archive`. State the approved lane set and boundaries, the number and limits of the mature Helio Start cohorts available then, why Helio Start was not ready on March 24, what acquisition evidence was still absent, and what the proposal gate did and did not authorize. Keep the comment historical.", "today": "2028-01-01", "tool": "post_doc_comment", "arguments": {"doc_id": "doc_q1_2026_board_archive", "body": "Historical correction — as of March 24, 2026:

The approved Q1 operating-evidence section contained three board-ready lanes, not four: Expansion Assist (descriptive only; 18 actual exposures, no randomized control, so no causal, revenue, or forecast claim); pricing-page path quality (post-November 26 rollout continuity, not a new causal test or revenue claim); and CS auto-nudge controls (system-control performance only). The lanes were to remain separate, each with its own denominator/coverage, limits, and claim scope. Helio Start was excluded from that section and was not board-ready.

By then, two consecutive mature Helio Start organic cohorts were available: 86 admitted workspaces and 91 admitted workspaces, each with complete day-90 windows. Both met the reopening evidence condition: fewer than 5% exceeded 90 support minutes (4/86, 4.7%; 3/91, 3.3%), and neither cohort had an unsupported case admitted. Their mature day-90 status, refund-adjusted cash, and account-level support effort were operating evidence from the organic path—not paid-acquisition results or proof of acquisition economics.

Helio Start remained not board-ready because the exact start and end dates for both cohorts were still absent, as required by the January 6 readiness gate. There had also been no paid traffic and no acquisition evidence: no paid-source outcomes or acquisition-cost comparison, and no controlled counterfactual. The two cohorts therefore did not support an acquisition, revenue, pipeline, or Q2 forecast claim.

The March 3 proposal gate, confirmed at the March 24 review, authorized preparation/consideration of a capped Q2 proposal only. It did not approve a budget, paid traffic or launch, acquisition authorization or claim, pipeline target/treatment, or forecast credit. Helio Start remained organic-only through March 31, 2026; any proposed test still required separate budget approval and the existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and support-routing rules to remain intact."}, "checks": [{"check_id": "riley_174_02", "path": "args", "criterion": "The comment says the approved Q1 section contained exactly three lanes, not Helio Start. It describes Expansion Assist as descriptive rather than causal evidence, pricing-page path quality as post-rollout continuity rather than a second causal test, and CS auto-nudge as system-control evidence. It says Helio Start was not board-ready at the March 24 review because its row lacked exact cohort start and end dates. It says two qualifying mature cohorts permitted only consideration of a capped proposal; there was no paid traffic, approved budget, or acquisition evidence; and the gate did not authorize paid traffic, budget, acquisition claims, pipeline treatment, or forecast credit. It does not claim that the March 24 decision establishes the status of those dates at a later time.", "value": {"doc_id": "doc_q1_2026_board_archive", "body": "Historical correction — as of March 24, 2026:

The approved Q1 operating-evidence section contained three board-ready lanes, not four: Expansion Assist (descriptive only; 18 actual exposures, no randomized control, so no causal, revenue, or forecast claim); pricing-page path quality (post-November 26 rollout continuity, not a new causal test or revenue claim); and CS auto-nudge controls (system-control performance only). The lanes were to remain separate, each with its own denominator/coverage, limits, and claim scope. Helio Start was excluded from that section and was not board-ready.

By then, two consecutive mature Helio Start organic cohorts were available: 86 admitted workspaces and 91 admitted workspaces, each with complete day-90 windows. Both met the reopening evidence condition: fewer than 5% exceeded 90 support minutes (4/86, 4.7%; 3/91, 3.3%), and neither cohort had an unsupported case admitted. Their mature day-90 status, refund-adjusted cash, and account-level support effort were operating evidence from the organic path—not paid-acquisition results or proof of acquisition economics.

Helio Start remained not board-ready because the exact start and end dates for both cohorts were still absent, as required by the January 6 readiness gate. There had also been no paid traffic and no acquisition evidence: no paid-source outcomes or acquisition-cost comparison, and no controlled counterfactual. The two cohorts therefore did not support an acquisition, revenue, pipeline, or Q2 forecast claim.

The March 3 proposal gate, confirmed at the March 24 review, authorized preparation/consideration of a capped Q2 proposal only. It did not approve a budget, paid traffic or launch, acquisition authorization or claim, pipeline target/treatment, or forecast credit. Helio Start remained organic-only through March 31, 2026; any proposed test still required separate budget approval and the existing eligibility, refusal, connector-access, external-authority, lifecycle, instrumentation, and support-routing rules to remain intact."}}]}

{"results":[{"check_id":"riley_174_02","passed":true,"reason":"The historical comment states there were “three board-ready lanes, not four,” excludes Helio Start, and accurately scopes Expansion Assist as “descriptive only,” pricing-page quality as “post-November 26 rollout continuity, not a new causal test,” and CS auto-nudge as “system-control performance only.” It says Helio Start was not board-ready because “the exact start and end dates for both cohorts were still absent,” identifies two consecutive mature cohorts, and limits the gate to “preparation/consideration of a capped Q2 proposal only.” It also states there was “no paid traffic and no acquisition evidence” or approved budget and expressly denies authorization of budget, paid traffic, acquisition claims, pipeline treatment, and forecast credit. The framing “as of March 24, 2026” keeps the correction historical and does not assert the dates remained absent later."}]}
